guide.title: User guide
guide.intro: Everything PortalGems can do, in one place.
guide.sendTitle: Send a file, a folder or a message
guide.sendBody: Under Send a file, choose a file, a whole folder, or write a message. The app shows a one-time code - give it to the other person. The transfer starts as soon as they enter it. A folder arrives as a folder, subfolders and all.
guide.receiveBody: Type the code the sender gave you and tap Receive. You see the name and size first, and can accept or decline. If something with that name already exists, you choose whether to overwrite it or keep both. A message is simply shown, ready to copy.
guide.pairTitle: Pair the devices you use often
guide.pairBody: Pair a new device links two devices once, so you never type a code between them again. Show a QR code on one and scan it with the other, or use a pairing code when there is no camera. Right after pairing you can give the device a name of your own and try a first transfer.
guide.devicesBody: Every paired device has Send and Receive buttons: one of you taps Send, the other taps Receive next to the sender's name. PortalGems must be open on both. Tap the device's name for more - send a folder, send a message, rename it or remove it. The device you used last is at the top, with the time of your last transfer.
guide.shareBody: In your gallery or file manager, choose Share and pick PortalGems. You can then send the file to one of your paired devices, or to anyone with a one-time code.
guide.dropBody: Drop a file or a folder onto a paired device in the list to send it there straight away.
guide.settingsBody: In Settings you can change the name this device gives when pairing, where received files are saved, the language and the color theme. You can also switch the connection server there - both devices must use the same one.
guide.serverBody: To start a transfer, the two devices first meet on a connection server. It only helps them find each other: everything is encrypted on your device, so the server never sees your files or messages. Settings > Connection server offers three: the PortalGems server (the default, recommended for reliability), the public magic-wormhole server run by the community, and a custom server you host yourself. Both devices must use the same server, or they will never meet. If transfers keep failing, try a different one on both.
guide.wormholeBody: PortalGems speaks the standard magic-wormhole protocol, so it works with the wormhole terminal program and other magic-wormhole apps. Those use the public server, so first switch to Public server in Settings > Connection server. Then send as usual and run wormhole receive on the computer with the code shown here - or run wormhole send there and type its code under Receive a file. Files, folders and messages all work. Pairing is a PortalGems feature, so use one-time codes with other apps. Switch back to the PortalGems server afterwards if your other devices use it.
guide.troubleTitle: If a transfer does not start
guide.troubleBody: Check that PortalGems is open on both devices and that both are online. Between paired devices, make sure both clocks show the right time - the devices use it to find each other. A one-time code works only once: if something went wrong, start the send again to get a fresh one.

explain.title: How it works
explain.intro: PortalGems uses the magic-wormhole protocol - an open standard for sending files safely from one device to another. Here is what happens under the hood, and why you can trust it.
explain.codesBody: Every transfer starts with a short one-time code like 7-crossover-clockwork. Both devices feed that code into a cryptographic handshake (SPAKE2) and derive the same strong encryption key from it. The code works exactly once: after a transfer - or after a single wrong guess - it becomes useless. An attacker would have to guess the entire code correctly on the very first try, and you would notice the failed attempt immediately.
explain.e2eBody: Your file is encrypted on your device and decrypted only on the receiving device. Everything in between - including the servers that help the two devices find each other - sees only unreadable ciphertext.
explain.directBody: When both devices are on the same Wi-Fi network, the file travels directly from one device to the other at full local speed - it never leaves your network. Only when a direct connection is impossible (for example, one device is on mobile data) does the transfer fall back to a public relay, which blindly forwards encrypted bytes it cannot read. Even then, the two devices still first meet at a mailbox server over the internet to run the handshake - so a direct connection is faster, but it is not an offline mode.
explain.serversBody: PortalGems keeps no user accounts and stores nothing about you. It relies on a mailbox server - where the two devices meet and confirm their encrypted handshake - and, when a direct connection is not possible, a relay that blindly forwards encrypted bytes. You choose which server to use in Settings: a public one, the PortalGems server, or your own. The mailbox is essential to the security model: without a server to broker the handshake, two devices have no way to find each other or agree on a key. So PortalGems always needs an internet connection and cannot work purely offline on a local network.
explain.pairingBody: When you pair two devices, they exchange one large random secret - via QR code or copy/paste - and store it in your device's protected storage. From then on, both devices can compute the same one-time code by themselves for every transfer, so you only confirm instead of typing. These derived codes are far stronger than typed codes, and they never leave your devices. Removing a paired device deletes the secret.
explain.limitsTitle: What this does not protect against
explain.limitsBody: Anyone who can see your screen while a code or pairing QR is visible can use it. Anyone with full access to your unlocked device can read what is stored on it. And an observer of your network can tell that you transferred something and roughly how large it was - but never what it was.
explain.choosingBody: PortalGems needs a mailbox server to introduce two devices, and you pick which one in Settings. The Public server is the community-run magic-wormhole one - it works with other wormhole apps but is occasionally unavailable. The PortalGems server is run by us and makes a reliable default. Custom lets you point the app at any server, including one you host yourself - see the self-hosting guide if you are interested. Whichever you choose, your files stay end-to-end encrypted and the server only ever sees scrambled data.

errors.title: Something went wrong
errors.pickFailed: Could not read the selected file.
errors.invalidCode: That does not look like a valid code. Codes look like: 7-word-word
errors.wrongCode: No file is being offered under this code. Double-check the code and make sure the sender's app is still open and waiting.
errors.network: Network problem - check your internet connection and try again.
errors.transit: The two devices could not open a connection to each other. Try again - if it keeps failing, check that both devices are online.
errors.peerGone: The other side went away before the transfer finished.
errors.declinedBySender: The transfer was declined or cancelled by the other side.
errors.serverUnreachable: Could not reach the connection server. It may be temporarily down. Open Settings and switch to the PortalGems server, or use your own - see the self-hosting guide.
errors.invalidServerUrl: The server address is not valid. Check it in Settings. A rendezvous URL looks like wss://host/v1 and a relay like tcp://host:4001.
